text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Debate warms up in ministries' budget negoatiations: various ministers have expressed anger at finance ministry plans to cut four billion markka from the budget frame already agreed.
- Amid debate on whether construction sector overheating, some argue subsidies on construction should be cut by less than the finance ministry planned.
- Finns have not shown great interest in international rapid deployment force -- army plans recruitment campaign next week. @
- Customs found 100,000 litres of contraband spirits on eastern border, in four trucks on the way to Moscow.
- Social and Health ministry has appointed a working group to study the development prospects of Finnish state owned Alko-group.
- International economists are at conference in Helsinki to discuss various trends in global economy.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Q2 results are expected to improve slightly from the first quarter. Forestry companies will post clearly better results towards year-end, analysts say. @
- Financial Supervision Authority says it cannot see any obstacles to cash withdrawal from retail cashiers with bank card.
- Company depreciation rules could be tightened and new tax on investments imposed, the finance ministry plans.
- Increased tourism to Finland has boosted tax free sales by 16 percent from last year.
AAMULEHTI
- Strengthening dollar, pound and yen versus the markka have increased state debt by 7.5 billion markka in first months. @
- Widening income differences are reasonable in current economic situation; moderate pay deal without great tax relief should be achieved, says Timo Relander, managing director at Statistics Finland.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Police should have rights to tap phones already at stage of crime prevention, Seppo Nevala, head of Security Police says.
- Cycle manufacturer Tunturi will not be sold in next couple of years, says company's owner Merita bank responding to comments from Swedish bicycle manufacturer Monark Stiga. @
DEMARI
- More cuts in construction would only damage sector already in bad employment situation, some socialist MPs say, wondering where finance ministry gets figures indicating it is overheating.
- Finnish development aid will be boosted substantially, development minister Pekka Haavisto says. -- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
